measured: the applications in scope (twin-world's demand/applications.json), each read at the commit the demand scan cloned (~/.cache/twin-demand), for @openrouter/sdk, @openrouter/ai-sdk-provider, openrouter.ai, its /api/v1 paths and OPENROUTER_ variables. Four call OpenRouter at run time: Substrate (vibecode's PKCE connection and the chat example), Volter Harness (its PKCE login, its key check and its model calls), Volter Editor (a person's OpenRouter credential checked, and the coding harnesses it points at OpenRouter on the BYOK route: Claude Code on the Anthropic Messages surface, Codex on the Responses API, OpenCode and Pi on chat completions) and LibreChat (an OpenRouter endpoint as its librechat.example.yaml configures it: the model list with its prices, and chat completions with OpenRouter's attribution headers). The platform's own callers: none (twin-world's packages, cookbook, scripts and architecture, and every other pack of twin-packs-p3, read apps/cloud carries the pack and the kernel's openaiWire names OpenRouter's fields, but nothing calls its hosts, doors or operations). Ruled out: localrouter (it serves OpenRouter's interface itself; @openrouter/sdk is a devDependency of its probes), Cal.com (@openrouter/ai-sdk-provider only in its lockfile, through another package), RH2 and Open Autonomy (their Hermes image disables its image_gen/openrouter plugin), Volter Browsers and Workbench (comments and docs only), Volter Editor's managed route (it calls Volter's generation gateway, not openrouter.ai), Twin (its own packs), Substrate's scripts/fixtures (test fixtures).

frontend.call: vibecode connects a person's OpenRouter account: the /auth page with a callback, an S256 challenge and key_label Vibecode
vibecode exchanges the code with its verifier for the person's key (through its gateway's relay)
the chat example's Pi streams chat completions on openai/gpt-4o

backend.call: login --oauth: the /auth page with an S256 challenge and key_label Volter Harness, with a loopback callback, or with none (--headless: the page shows the code to paste)
the code exchanged with its verifier for a key
after login and in doctor: the key checked by GET /key (OpenRouter's catalogue needs no key)
the harness's model calls: chat completions, streamed with usage (stream_options.include_usage), tools, reasoning_effort, reasoning.max_tokens, response_format

applications.name: volter-ai/editor
applications.client: its fetch; the coding harnesses it launches (Claude Code, Codex, OpenCode, Pi)

backend.call: a person's OpenRouter credential is checked when saved: GET /key
BYOK coding: Claude Code with ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL https://openrouter.ai/api and the key as ANTHROPIC_AUTH_TOKEN: Anthropic Messages, streamed
BYOK coding: Codex with wire_api responses at https://openrouter.ai/api/v1: the Responses API, streamed
BYOK coding: OpenCode's and Pi's openrouter provider: chat completions, streamed, on z-ai/glm-5.2 (the default coding model)

applications.name: LibreChat-AI/LibreChat
applications.client: axios (the model list); the OpenAI client through its custom endpoint (chat)

backend.call: the OpenRouter endpoint's models fetched (models.fetch: true), each model's pricing read into its token config
a conversation and its title on the OpenRouter endpoint: chat completions, streamed, with HTTP-Referer, X-Title and X-OpenRouter-Title

standIns: a key is made on Settings > Keys, and a person signs in at openrouter.ai (the doors); a turn is the World's scenario's, else a labeled stub: the twin runs no model; the catalogue is the models the applications name, at the prices openrouter.ai's model pages state.
notDemanded: model endpoints, credits, generation stats, embeddings, keys management, guardrails, BYOK, files, batches, presets, workspaces and the rest: no application here calls them.
